full_judgment: 5. Upazilla Nirbahi Officer Gomostapur issued an order under section 144 of the Code of apprehension of breach of peace over the possession of disputed Akhra and its properties between the second party petitioner Shebait Mohanta Sree Kedar Nath Achari and 1st party opposite party No 1 Sree Khitish Chandra Bhattacharya @ Achri. Thereafter on 22-4-91 Officer-in-Charge Gomostapu PS submitted a report to the Upazila Magistrate to draw up a proceeding under section 145 by the said court as in spite of service of notice under section 154 of the penal Code and arrest of the petitioner and opposite party No 1 situation could not be controlled. On the basis of the said report on 22-4-91 Upazilia Magistrate attached all the properties of the Akhra and appointed two receivers who took over possession on 24-4-91. Thereafter petitioner moved this court on 29-5-91 10 Criminal Revision No-783 of 1991 and obtained Rule, order-of stay and also to continue to function as Mohanta of the said properties. Thereafter on 6-6-91 in pursuance of the aforesaid order, petitioner got possession of the said properties from the receivers. Thereafter on 22-1-96 the said Rule was discharged and order of stay vacated. Thereafter on 6-8-97 Magistrate directed the petitioner to hand over charge to the receiver petitioner who filed an application for vacating the said order which was rejected on 26-11-96. Thereafter on 19-1-98 petitioner again moved this court in Criminal Revision No 25 of 1998 and obtained a Rule, order of stay and also to continue to function as the Mohanta of the said properties. The said Rule was discharged on 19-3-98 and stay was vacated. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner moved the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition no-96 of 1998 and the same was dismissed on 4-6-98 Thereafter receivers took over possession from the petitioner. Thereafter by judgment and order dated 25-10-98 Magistrate. 1st Class, Nawabganj declared possession in favour of the petitioner and receiver was directed to hand over possession to him. Being aggrieved by the same 1st party opposite party No. 1 filed Criminal Revision No 61 of 1998 before the Sessions Judge who stayed the operation of the judgment and order of the learned Magistrate. After hearing both the parties learned Additional Sessions Judge allowed the said revision by the impugned judgment dated 28-2-99. By the Impugned judgment and order of the learned Magistrate was set aside and the receiver was directed to hand over possession to the 2nd party opposite party No 1. Thereafter on 10-3-99 Magistrate directed the receivers to make over the possession to the 1st party opposite party No. 1 and accordingly on 12-3-99 and 21-3-99 possession was handed over to him.
